text:
# Aadhaar Enrolment
Learn about the Aadhaar enrolment process, required documents, biometric capture and enrolment options available across India free of cost.
Process
The Aadhaar enrolment process includes visiting Enrolment Centre, filling the enrolment form, getting demographic and biometric data captured, submitting proof of Identity and address documents, before collecting acknowledgement slip containing Enrolment ID. The highlights of Aadhaar enrolment are:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Aadhaar enrolment is free of cost.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
You can go to any authorized [Aadhaar enrolment centre](https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/) anywhere in India with your proof of identity and proof of address documents
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
UIDAI process accepts **wide range of PoI (Proof of Identity) and PoA (Proof of Address) documents. Document:- PDF Size:-1.6 M** View the [list of supporting documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf). Common proofs of identity and address are election photo ID card, Ration card, passport and driving license.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Photo ID cards like Voter Card and Govt ID cards are permissible for identity proof. Address proof documents also include water - electricity - Landline telephone bills for the last three months.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Certificate of Address having photo issued by MP or MLA /Gazetted Officer/Tehsildar on letterhead or by Village Panchayat head or its equivalent authority (for rural areas) is accepted as valid PoA. Even if someone in a family does not have individual valid documents, the the individual seeking to enrol can still enrol if his/her name exists in family entitlement document. In this case the **Head of Family** mentioned in entitlement document needs to be enrolled first with valid PoI & PoA document. The head of the Family can then introduce other members in the family while they are enrolling. UIDAI accepts many document types as Proof of Relationship. Please [View the list of supporting documents. Document:- PDF Size:-1.6 MB](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf).

**To summarise, there are two approaches for enrolment:**
**Document Based**
Submission of one valid Proof of Identity (PoI) document and one valid Proof of Address(PoA) document
**Head Of Family (Hof)-based**
Head of family (HoF) may introduce family members by means of documents, which establish the Proof of Relationship (PoR).
![Card image](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/capturing_demographic_and_biometric_1.webp)
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
You need to enrol only once, as multiple enrolments will result in rejections unless it is advised by UIDAI.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The waiting time for Aadhaar is 180 days after receipt of **enrolment** data packets in CIDR.

Where to Enrol
Enrolment in all the states/UTs is being covered by UIDAI. **Individuals** of all states/UTs **seeking enrolment** , are required to enrol **only at** nearby [Aadhaar Enrolment Centre/Aadhaar Camps](https://bookappointment.uidai.gov.in/).
![Information](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/Info.svg)

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_a9e0d1e4
text:
### 
How to download the Aadhaar app?
You can download the Aadhaar app on your Android/iOS device from the Play Store/App Store. For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/aadhaar/id6744029871

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_a9e0d1e4
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_a9e0d1e4
text:
### 
Which services are available on this app?
Presently, the Aadhaar app offers various services like - Mobile Number Update, Address Update, Biometric lock/unlock, Selective Sharing of Aadhaar Verifiable Credential, check Authentication History, download e-Aadhaar, share Contact Card, Track my request, etc.
[View more F.A.Qs](https://uidai.gov.in/en/faq)

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b4926121
text:
# OVSE
Find answers to frequently asked questions about the Offline Verification Seeking Entity (OVSE) framework, including registration requirements, technical specifications, onboarding process, Aadhaar offline verification methods, use cases, compliance obligations, integration guidelines, security features, and support resources for organizations seeking secure, consent-based identity verification without connecting to UIDAI’s CIDR.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b4926121
text:
### 
OVSE
![expand](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/AccordionArrow.svg)
How can an entity become a registered OVSE?
An entity willing to became OVSE may submit the application through https://ovse.uidai.gov.in/. UIDAI may register the entity as a registered OVSE, after verification of the submitted details.
Can registered OVSE collect and store my verifiable credentials?
Yes. A registered OVSE may collect and store verifiable credentials shared with the explicit consent of the Aadhaar Number Holder.
Can offline verification be performed on behalf of another entity?
No. Offline verification cannot be performed on behalf of another entity.
What details are required for onboarding on the Aadhaar app?
The ANH should have a smartphone (Android version 9.0 and above and iOS version 16.0 and above) with internet connectivity.
What is an Aadhaar Verifiable Credential in the context of the Aadhaar App?
An Aadhaar Verifiable Credential is a digitally signed document issued by the Authority to the Aadhaar Number Holder. It may contain the last 4 digits of the Aadhaar number, demographic data such as name, address, gender, date of birth, and photograph of the Aadhaar Number Holder, and such other information as may be specified by the Authority. These credentials may be shared by the Aadhaar Number Holder, in full or in part, with an OVSE in the manner specified by the Authority, for verifying the demographic information or the photograph of the Aadhaar Number Holder.
Does an entity need a specific SDK from UIDAI to generate QR codes, or is there a different approach?
No SDK is required. The OVSE must follow the QR generation guidelines issued by UIDAI. A registered OVSE may contact UIDAI for any technical support related to QR generation.
Whether an OVSE can request and receive the last 4 digits of Aadhaar number through the Aadhaar App from an Aadhaar Number Holder?
Yes, the OVSE is permitted to request and receive the last 4 digits of the Aadhaar number from Aadhaar Number Holder as part of the Aadhaar Verified Credentials through the Aadhaar App.
[The Terms and Conditions shall continue to apply on OVSE including the following provisions of The Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies. Benefits and Services) Act, 2016:
Section 8A (3) An offline verification -seeking entity shall inform the individual undergoing the offline verification, or in case of a child, his parent or guardian, the following details with respect to offline verification, in such manner as may be specified by regulations, namely:-- 
  1. the nature of information that may be shared upon offline verification;
  2. the uses to which the information received during offline verification may be put by the offline verification-seeking entity; and
  3. alternatives to submission of information requested for, if any. ]  

Can Offline Aadhaar data collected by registered OVSE be shared by respective OVSE with another entity?
Offline Aadhaar data collected by registered OVSE can be shared by respective OVSE with another entity subject to the following conditions
  1. the identity of each recipient and the specific verification purpose (e.g., loan application verification) are expressly disclosed in writing to the ANH at the time of offline verification;
  2. the ANH gives granular, informed consent to such onward sharing; and
  3. upon revocation of consent by ANH, OVSE shall ensure in a verifiable manner, end‑to‑end deletion of offline Aadhaar data and provide acknowledgement of the same to ANH.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b49dde8f
text:
# Updating Data on Aadhaar
Biometric devices are instruments, designed to capture biometric data inputs including fingerprint and iris information from Aadhaar number holders for the purpose of authentication and identity verification.
Registered Mobile Number
**Registered mobile number is essential to access Aadhaar Online Services**
You can verify your mobile number that has been declared at the time of enrolment or during latest Aadhaar detail update.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
[Verify your mobile number](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/verify-email-mobile/en)

If you have not registered your Mobile number while enrolling for Aadhaar, you are **required to visit a**
Enabling Aadhaar for various services like Government & Non-Government Services, Subsidy Benefits, Pensions, Scholarships, Social Benefits, Banking services, Insurance services, Taxation services, Education, Employment, Healthcare etc., makes it essential to ensure that Aadhaar data of the Aadhaar number holder stored in the CIDR is accurate and up-to-date.
Demographic data update, the need could arise from:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Changes in life events such as marriage may lead to Aadhaar number holders changing their basic demographic details such as name and address. Address and mobile number could also change due to migration to newer locations. Aadhaar number holders may also want changes in their relative’s details due to changes in life events such marriage, death of a relative etc. In addition, Aadhaar number holders could have other personal reasons to change their mobile number, email address etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Changes in various service delivery platforms may lead Aadhaar number holders to declaration request changes and to add mobile number to CIDR etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Errors made during the enrolment process wherein the demographic data of individuals seeking to enrol may have been captured incorrectly.Changes to “DoB/Age” and “Gender” fields are expected primarily due to enrolment errors.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Since an individual can enrol anywhere in India, it may happen that a native speaker of language "A" is enrolled by an operator of language "B" and consequently the individual’s local language of enrolment is "B". Later, the Aadhaar number holder may want to change the local language of enrolment to another that he/she prefers. If so, then all the demographic information that is printed on the Aadhaar letter will need to be updated in the new local language.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
UIDAI may also ascertain availability of POI, POA and other documents collected at the time of enrolment/update and its quality and decide to notify Aadhaar number holder to update their demographic information and submit the required document.

Biometric update, the need could arise from:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age <5 years at the time of initial enrolment** -The child should be re-enroled when the child attains an age of 5 years and all biometric data should be provided. A de-duplication would be done for the child at this stage. This request will be treated similar to a new enrolment request while retaining the original Aadhaar number
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age between 5 and 15 years at the time of enrolment** - The Aadhaar number holder should furnish all biometrics for updates when he/she attains age of 15 years.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age >15 years at the time of enrolment** – Aadhaar number holders are recommended to update their biometric data every 10 years.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Events like accidents or diseases leading to biometric exception
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
As the Aadhaar authentication service is becoming ubiquitous, Aadhaar number holders may also approach for biometric updates because of authentication failures (called false rejects – where a correct Aadhaar number holder with valid Aadhaar number may be incorrectly rejected) which may result from incorrect biometric capture or poor biometric quality captured at the time of enrolment. With improvements in technology, it may be possible to capture better quality biometrics in the CIDR.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
UIDAI may verify the **quality** of biometrics captured during enrolment/ update and decide a threshold quality. All Aadhaar number holders with biometrics below the threshold level would/**will** be notified by UIDAI to update their biometrics

Aadhaar details that can be updated are:  
| Demographic Information  | Name, Address, Date of Birth/Age, Gender, Mobile Number, Email Address, Relationship Status and Information Sharing Consent  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Biometric Information  | Iris, Finger Prints and Facial Photograph  |  
UIDAI update process accepts wide range of PoI (Proof of Identity) and PoA (Proof of Address) documents. View the [List of supporting documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF SIze: 1.6MB.**
Modes of Update
1. Via Online
  
The online mode offers address update to the Aadhaar number holders where the Aadhaar number holder can directly place the address update request on the myAadhaar portal. The Aadhaar number holder needs to have mobile number registered with Aadhaar for using this service. The Aadhaar number is required to login to the [portal](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/) by the Aadhaar number holder. The Aadhaar number holder is authenticated using sent OTP on his/her registered mobile number. To complete the update process, Aadhaar number holder needs to upload the [supporting POA documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF Size: 1.6MB** , which will be verified against requested data at a later stage by a quality and processing team.
By Visiting Aadhaar Enrolment Centre
Aadhaar number holders place the demographic/biometric update request with the help of an operator at an [Aadhaar Enrolment Centre](https://appointments.uidai.gov.in/easearch.aspx). In such a case, the documentary evidence is collected by the operator at the time of accepting the request. The document verification by the verifier also happens at the time of placing the update request. UIDAI currently has envisaged three modes for Assisted Updates:
a. Update Client Standard
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Fields** : All biometric and demographic fields as well as local language can be updated
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Identity Authentication** : Biometric check at the back-end.

Document Verification
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Enrolment / Update Centre.

Form Filling and Acknowledgement
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Handles spelling, language issues, transliteration, etc. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Update Request Number (URN) which can be tracked.
![Card image](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/update_client_standard.webp)
b. Update Client Lite (UCL)
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Fields** : All demographic fields and Photo as well as local language can be updated.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Identity Authentication** : Biometric Authentication of Aadhaar number holder.

Document Verification
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Aadhaar Enrolment / Update Centre.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The verification procedure followed should be in line with DDSVP Committee Recommendations followed during enrolment process

Form Filling in software and Acknowledgement
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Enrolment ID (EID) which can be used for checking status. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b49dde8f
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

This can be verified by using the below public key

string XMLFilePath = ""; //Get the XML file string KeyFilePath = ""; //Get the public key certificate file XmlDocument ObjXmlDocument = new XmlDocument(); ObjXmlDocument.Load(XMLFilePath); //Load the XML XmlAttributeCollection SignatureElement = ObjXmlDocument.DocumentElement.Attributes; //Get the all XML attribute string SignatureValue = SignatureElement.GetNamedItem("s").InnerXml; // Get Signature value SignatureElement.RemoveNamedItem("s");//Remove the signature "s" attribute from XML and get the new XML to validate /*----------------Read and parse the public key as string-----------------------*/ X509Certificate2 ObjX509Certificate2 = new X509Certificate2(KeyFilePath, "public"); //Initialize the public ket certificate file Org.BouncyCastle.X509.X509Certificate objX509Certificate; X509CertificateParser objX509CertificateParser = new X509CertificateParser(); objX509Certificate = objX509CertificateParser.ReadCertificate(ObjX509Certificate2.GetRawCertData()); /*----------------End-----------------------*/ /* Init alg */ ISigner signer = SignerUtilities.GetSigner("SHA256withRSA"); /* Populate key */ signer.Init(false, objX509Certificate.GetPublicKey()); /* Get the signature into bytes */ var expectedSig = Convert.FromBase64String(SignatureValue); /* Get the bytes to be signed from the string */ var msgBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(ObjXmlDocument.InnerXml); /* Calculate the signature and see if it matches */ signer.BlockUpdate(msgBytes, 0, msgBytes.Length); bool Flag = signer.VerifySignature(expectedSig); if (Flag) { MessageBox.Show("XML Validate Successfully"); } else { MessageBox.Show("XML Validation Failed"); }

Developing in C/C++
**NOTE: This code is contributed by Geodesic team and is available on as-is basis. Sample C application to test Aadhaar authentication can be downloaded****.**  
  
A sample C client with source code is provided to help the community rapidly develop applications that use Aadhaar authentication. This sample application is written in C for the GeoAmida device and it demonstrates various features of Aadhaar authentication. This application is provided on an "AS-IS" basis and should not be considered as a supported, production strength software. This chapter covers details about downloading and setting up development environment.  
  
**Setting up Development Environment**  
  
When you download the source distribution from the link above, you get "c-auth-client-source-1.5.zip". Please follow steps below to setup the client as a development environment. These directions are for Linux OS and ARM devices. If you are using Windows or other OS, you may make appropriate modification to the instructions below.   
  
Unzip "c-auth-client-source-1.5.zip" into a directory. You should now see a directory named "c-auth-client-source-1.5" there  
  
Navigate to "c-auth-client-source-1.5" directory. You should see the following listing.
![Directory Listing](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/dir-list.webp)
**Dependency Libraries** :  
libxml >= 2.7.6  
openssl >= 0.9.8  
**Digital Signature Generation requires an additional libraries** :  
libXslt >= 1.1.24  
libxmlsec1 >= 1.2.9
The below DEFINES values are need to modify before compiling:  
LICENCE_KEY  
UIDAI_PUBLIC_CERITIFICATE  
AUA_PRIVATE_CERTIFICATE - Required for Digital Signature
Auth Xml API documentation is available under the doc folder
![API Functions](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/auth-xml-apis.webp)
You may use any editor tool (Eclipse, emacs or vim) installed on your development machine and setup the environment variable, LD_LIBRARY_PATH in order to find libraries.
Within "Command Prompt", change directory ("cd") to "c-auth-client-source-1.5
Sample Makefile included in the build for Geoamida and gcc version.  
`CC = arm-xscale-linux-gnueabi-gcc`
On a successful make, you should see the executable file AuthClient.
Run AuthClient. It will generate Auth-XML. During compilation if the "-D XML_SECURITY" flag is set, then the Digital Signature will be created along with Auth Xml.
Developing using Sample Applications
As explained in previous chapter, sample Java client with source code is provided to help the community rapidly develop applications that use Aadhaar authentication. This application is written in Java and demonstrates various features of Aadhaar authentication. This application is provided on an "AS-IS" basis and should not be considered as a supported, production strength software. This chapter covers details about downloading and setting up development environment.
Sample Java application (both binary and source code zip files) to test Aadhaar authentication can be [**downloaded from here**](https://uidai.gov.in/data-and-download).  
  
**Setting up Development Environment**
When you download the source distribution using downlink above, you get "auth-client-source-1.5.zip". Follow steps below to setup the client as a development environment. These directions are for Windows OS. If you are using Linux or other OS, you may make appropriate modification to the instructions below.  
  
You need
**Java 1.6.20 or above, Apache Maven 2.2.1 or above, and Eclipse Java IDE installed on your computer** to setup environment based on this page.
You can use the source code and setup environment if you want it in other IDEs and build environments.
Unzip "auth-client-source-1.5.zip" into a directory. You should now see a directory named "auth-client-source-1.5" there
Navigate to "auth-client-source-1.5" directory. You should see the following listing.  

![Setting up Development Environment](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/source_dir_screen.webp)
Within "Command Prompt", change directory ("cd") to "auth-client-source-1.5"
Run "mvn eclipse:eclipse" command. If "Maven\bin" is not in path, please add it. Otherwise "mvn" command will not run.
You should see "Build Successful" message like below.
![Setting up Development Environment](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/cmd_screen.webp)
Launch Eclipse and create a new workspace (or use current workspace if you prefer)
Choose "File->Import" menu. This lanuches an import dialog.
Choose "Existing Projects into Workspace" option and click "Next"
Click "Browse" button next to "Select Root Directory"
Navigate to "auth-client-source-1.5" and select the directory
This will list 4 projects - "uidai-auth-client", "uidai-auth-xsd-model", "uidai-biometric-integration-api", and "uidai-sample-gui-app"
Make sure all projects are selected. See screen below.
![Setting up Development Environment](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/eclipse_import_screen.webp)
Click "Finish" to import all 4 projects into workspace
If you have project that provides biometric integration API implementation, you will have to add it to the class path of the "uidai-sample-gui-app" project.Also, update the value of field, biometricAPIImplementationClass, in the SampleClientMainFrame.java to the value of the class that implements the API.
Select "SampleClientMainFrame.java" under project "uidai-sample-gui-app" (src/main/java/in/gov/uidai/auth/sampleapp folder) and choose "Run->Run Configurations" menu or click "Run" icon on toolbar and choose "Run Configurations".
![Setting up Development Environment](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/eclipse_run_config_create.webp)
Click "New Launch Configuration" icon on left top corner within the dialog. This created a new default run configuration for the sample application.
In order to use Indian name matching, it is required that the java apps run in UTF-8 character encoding mode. For that, in Java, following VM arguments has to be passed "-Dfile.encoding=UTF8". Within "Run Configurations" doalog, add this to VM arguments
![Setting up Development Environment](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/eclipse_run_config_dlg.webp)
Click "Run" button on the bottom right within the "Run Configuration" dialog to run the application. you should see the sample application GUI window.
Choose "Edit->Preferences" menu option and ensure you choose appropriate path for public key file and keystore file (they are available under "auth-client-source-1.5\uidai-auth-client\src\main\resources" folder. Ensure license key, AUA code, Sub AUA code are as listed under "Testing Data" page
Enter "999999990019" in "Aadhaar Number" field and "Shivshankar Choudhury" in the "Name" field. Additional data is available on "Testing Data" page.
Click "Authenticate" button at the bottom right
You should see a green tick mark within the "Authentication Status" field. See the following screen
![](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/auth_client_result_screen.webp)
If you have issues, first ensure you have followed all steps correctly. If you face network or connection errors, please make sure your Internet connection is working well. If test server (auth.uidai.gov.in) is down or not reachable, try after some time.
If nothing works (!), please write to the Discussion Forum Page
Running Sample Application
UIDAI has created a fully working sample Java client application to help the community rapidly develop applications that use Aadhaar authentication. This application is written in Java and demonstrates various features of Aadhaar authentication. This application is provided on an "AS-IS" basis and should not be considered as a supported, production strength software. This chapter covers details about downloading, installing, and running the sample and setting up development environment with the source code.
Sample Java application (both binary and source code zip files) to test Aadhaar authentication can be [downloaded from here](https://uidai.gov.in/data-and-downloads).  
  
**Running Sample from Distribution**
When you download the binary distribution using downlink above, you get "auth-client-bin-1.5.zip". Follow steps below to install and run the client. These directions are for Windows OS. If you are using Linux or other OS, you may make appropriate modification to build and run the client.
**You need Java 1.6 or above installed on your computer and an Internet connection to run this sample.**
Unzip "auth-client-bin-1.5.zip" into a directory. You will see the following contents.
![Sample Client Runtime Directory Listing](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/auth_sample_dir_listing.webp)
Run "runclient.bat" to run the sample application.
In order to use Indian name matching, it is required that the java apps run in UTF-8 character encoding mode. For that, in Java, following VM arguments has to be passed "-Dfile.encoding=UTF8". This is already added to the "runclient.bat" file.
This opens a command promt asking for OS type, enter 1 or 2 (based on your OS) and press ENTER.
This opens the sample authentication client. See screenshot below.
![](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/auth_client_main_screen.webp)
Click "Edit->Preferences" menu to make sure you see following screen with values. **Ensure license key, AUA code, Sub AUA code are as listed under "Testing Data" page.**
![](https://www.uidai.gov.in/images/authDoc/auth_client_pref_screen.jpg)
Now you are ready to test!!
Enter "999999990019" in "Aadhaar Number" field and "Shivshankar Choudhury" in the "Name" field. See "Testing Data" page for details on test data for testing various combinations.
Click "Authenticate" button at the bottom right
You should see a green tick mark within the "Authentication Status" field. See the following screen
![](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-07/auth_client_result_screen.webp)
If you have issues, first ensure you have followed all steps correctly. If you face network or connection errors, please make sure your Internet connection is working well. If test server (auth.uidai.gov.in) is down or not reachable, try after some time.
If nothing works (!), please write to the Discussion Forum Page.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b8f1d94e
text:
### 
UIDAI Finance & Accounts Division
![expand](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/AccordionArrow.svg)
The Finance & Accounts Division (FD) is headed by the Deputy Director General (Finance) who is Financial Advisor in UIDAI. FD renders professional advice to the CEO, UIDAI on all issues which have financial implications.
The FD is responsible for Budget formulation, Outcome Budget, Performance Budget, Screening of proposals involving financial implications, Expenditure and Cash Management and Preparation of Annual Accounts of UIDAI.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b8f1d94e
text:
### 
Role of Finance & Accounts Division
![expand](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/AccordionArrow.svg)
**Financial Advice/Concurrence**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Associating with policy and program formulation activities to facilitate proper appreciation of the financial implications.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Advice on delegation of financial powers;
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Financial advice on all matters involving expenditure/concurrence to financial proposals for Acceptance of Necessity (AON) and Expenditure Angle Sanction (EAS) of Competent Authority.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Vetting of tender/RFP documents, contracts including amendment of contract from financial angle.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Scrutiny of and concurrence to foreign deputation proposals of officers of UIDAI
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Representation in various committees (CAB, Tender opening and Financial Evaluation Committee, Commercial Negotiation Committees, Other Committees) and
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Internal control systems by way of Procurement Manual to ensure ‘Due Diligence’ and compliance of rules and regulations and guidelines of the Ministry of Finance in respect of various procurements and contracts.

**Budget preparation**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Preparation of Budget and related work (Budget Estimate, Revised Estimate and Supplementary Grants, re-appropriation, etc.) and
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Allocation of budget among Functional Divisions at HQ and Regional Offices

**Drawing & Disbursement**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Payment of salary and allowances to employees of HQ.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Payment of salary and allowances to employees of RO.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Payment and settlement of personal claims of employees and
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Payment of all types of bills for goods and services received from suppliers.

**Book keeping**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Maintenance of all books of accounts and preparation of monthly, quarterly and annual financial statements and
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Maintenance of Fixed Asset Register and depreciation accounting.

**Expenditure and Cash Management**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Monitoring and control of expenditure and accounting functions of HQ and ROs.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Maintenance of PBG register and safe custody of PBG.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Bank reconciliation and
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Investment of surplus funds and safe custody of instruments thereof.

**Internal Audit**
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b8f1d94e
text:
### 
How to download the Aadhaar app?
You can download the Aadhaar app on your Android/iOS device from the Play Store/App Store. For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/aadhaar/id6744029871

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b8f1d94e
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_b8f1d94e
text:
### 
Which services are available on this app?
Presently, the Aadhaar app offers various services like - Mobile Number Update, Address Update, Biometric lock/unlock, Selective Sharing of Aadhaar Verifiable Credential, check Authentication History, download e-Aadhaar, share Contact Card, Track my request, etc.

text:
### 
How to download the Aadhaar app?
You can download the Aadhaar app on your Android/iOS device from the Play Store/App Store. For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/aadhaar/id6744029871

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_ba69194b
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_ba69194b
text:
### 
Which services are available on this app?
Presently, the Aadhaar app offers various services like - Mobile Number Update, Address Update, Biometric lock/unlock, Selective Sharing of Aadhaar Verifiable Credential, check Authentication History, download e-Aadhaar, share Contact Card, Track my request, etc.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_bc509fbe
text:
# Usage of Aadhaar
The Government of India, as well as the State Governments, fund a number of social welfare schemes and programs that are focused on the poor and most vulnerable sections of society. Aadhaar and its platform offer a unique opportunity for the government to streamline its delivery mechanism under welfare schemes, thereby ensuring transparency and efficiency. The use of Aadhaar as an identity document enables beneficiaries to get their entitlements directly in a convenient and seamless/hassle free manner by obviating the need to produce multiple documents to prove one’s identity.
For Governments, Service Agencies
UIDAI issues Aadhaar numbers to the individuals seeking to enroll, only after de-duplicating their demographic and biometric attributes against its entire database. Aadhaar seeding enables elimination of duplicates under various schemes which leads to substantial savings to the government exchequers. It also provides the government with accurate data on the beneficiaries and enables implementation of direct benefit transfer (DBT) programmes. Aadhaar authentication enables the implementing agencies to verify the beneficiaries at the time of service/benefits delivery and also ensures the targeted delivery of benefits to them. All these activities will lead to:-
**Curbing Leakages through Targeted Delivery:** All social welfare programmes where beneficiaries are required to be confirmed before the service delivery, stand to benefit from UIDAI’s authentication services. This will result in curbing leakages and ensuring that services are delivered to the intended beneficiaries only. Examples include subsidized food and kerosene delivery to Public Distribution System (PDS) beneficiaries, worksite attendance of Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (MGNREGS) beneficiaries, etc.
**Improving Efficiency and Efficacy:** With the Aadhaar platform providing accurate and transparent information about the service delivery mechanism, government can improve disbursement systems and utilize its scarce development funds more effectively and efficiently.
For Aadhaar number holders
Aadhaar system provides single source offline/online identity verification across the country for the Aadhaar number holders. Once Aadhaar number holders enroll, they can use their Aadhaar number to authenticate and establish their identity multiple times using electronic means or through offline verification, as the case may be. It eliminates the hassle of repeatedly providing supporting identity documents each time a Aadhaar number holder wishes to access services, benefits or subsidies. Since Aadhaar is universal identity accepted across the whole country, the Aadhaar system enables mobility to millions of people who migrate from one part of the country to another by providing a portable proof of identity that can be verified through Aadhaar authentication on-line anytime, anywhere.

### 
How to download the Aadhaar app?
You can download the Aadhaar app on your Android/iOS device from the Play Store/App Store. For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/aadhaar/id6744029871

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_bf96de1f
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_bf96de1f
text:
### 
Which services are available on this app?
Presently, the Aadhaar app offers various services like - Mobile Number Update, Address Update, Biometric lock/unlock, Selective Sharing of Aadhaar Verifiable Credential, check Authentication History, download e-Aadhaar, share Contact Card, Track my request, etc.

Authentication devices play a vital role in the Aadhaar authentication ecosystem by securely capturing, encrypting and transmitting Personal Identity Data (PID) for verification. These devices include desktops, laptops, kiosks, Point-of-Sale (PoS) systems, handheld microATMs and tablets, enabling seamless and secure authentication services across multiple platforms and use cases.

How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

text: ## Frequently Asked Questions

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: What are the different forms of Aadhaar and what are their features?
text:
### What are the different forms of Aadhaar and what are their features?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
The different forms of Aadhaar are Aadhaar Letter, Aadhaar PVC card, eAadhaar and mAadhaar. All forms of Aadhaar are equally valid and acceptable.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: Can I choose to have and use any form of Aadhaar?
text:
### Can I choose to have and use any form of Aadhaar?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
Yes

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: What is “Order Aadhaar PVC Card” service?
text:
### What is “Order Aadhaar PVC Card” service?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
“Order Aadhaar PVC Card” is an online service launched by UIDAI which facilitates the Aadhaar holder to get their Aadhaar details printed on PVC card by paying nominal charges.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: What are the security features of “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
text:
### What are the security features of “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
This card contains security features like:
  * Tamper proof QR Code
  * Micro text
  * Ghost image
  * Issue Date & Print Date
  * Guilloche Pattern
  * Embossed Aadhaar Logo

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: What are the charges to be paid for “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
text:
### What are the charges to be paid for “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
Charges to be paid are Rs.75/- (Inclusive of GST & speed post charges).

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: How one can raise the request for “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
text:
### How one can raise the request for “Aadhaar PVC Card”?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
''Aadhaar PVC Card' request can be raised by visiting the UIDAI Official Website ([https://www.uidai.gov.in](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/`https:/www.uidai.gov.in`) or https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in) or mAadhaar application

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_cf7ba17a
section: How to raise request using Registered Mobile Number?
text:
### How to raise request using Registered Mobile Number?
![](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/static/media/ArrowDown.a5229ab197c918ede75c7ae811502301.svg)
Please Visit https://uidai.gov.in or https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in.
  * Click on Login, Enter your 12-digit Aadhaar Number (UID).
  * Enter the security code
  * Click on “Login with OTP” button. 
  * Enter OTP received on registered mobile number.
  * Click on 'Order Aadhaar PVC Card' tile.
  * On next screen, select option 'Order Aadhaar PVC Card for Self', preview of the Aadhaar details will appear for verification by Aadhaar number holder before placing the order for Aadhaar PVC Card.
  * Click on the check box against “Terms and Conditions”. (Note: Click on hyper link to see details).
  * Click on “Submit” Button to complete OTP verification. 
  * Click on “Make payment”. You will be re-directed to Payment Gateway page with payment options as Credit/Debit Card, Net banking and UPI.
  * After successful payment, receipt will get generated having digital signature which can be downloaded by Aadhaar number holder in PDF format. Aadhaar number holder will also get the Service Request Number via SMS.
  * Aadhaar number holder can track the status of SRN till dispatch of Aadhaar Card on Check Aadhaar Card Status.
  * SMS containing AWB number will also be sent once dispatched from DoP. Aadhaar number holder can further track delivery status by visiting DoP website.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_d12ba00a
text:
# Updating Data on Aadhaar
Biometric devices are instruments, designed to capture biometric data inputs including fingerprint and iris information from Aadhaar number holders for the purpose of authentication and identity verification.
Registered Mobile Number
**Registered mobile number is essential to access Aadhaar Online Services**
You can verify your mobile number that has been declared at the time of enrolment or during latest Aadhaar detail update.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
[Verify your mobile number](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/verify-email-mobile/en)

If you have not registered your Mobile number while enrolling for Aadhaar, you are **required to visit a**
Enabling Aadhaar for various services like Government & Non-Government Services, Subsidy Benefits, Pensions, Scholarships, Social Benefits, Banking services, Insurance services, Taxation services, Education, Employment, Healthcare etc., makes it essential to ensure that Aadhaar data of the Aadhaar number holder stored in the CIDR is accurate and up-to-date.
Demographic data update, the need could arise from:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Changes in life events such as marriage may lead to Aadhaar number holders changing their basic demographic details such as name and address. Address and mobile number could also change due to migration to newer locations. Aadhaar number holders may also want changes in their relative’s details due to changes in life events such marriage, death of a relative etc. In addition, Aadhaar number holders could have other personal reasons to change their mobile number, email address etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Changes in various service delivery platforms may lead Aadhaar number holders to declaration request changes and to add mobile number to CIDR etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Errors made during the enrolment process wherein the demographic data of individuals seeking to enrol may have been captured incorrectly.Changes to “DoB/Age” and “Gender” fields are expected primarily due to enrolment errors.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Since an individual can enrol anywhere in India, it may happen that a native speaker of language "A" is enrolled by an operator of language "B" and consequently the individual’s local language of enrolment is "B". Later, the Aadhaar number holder may want to change the local language of enrolment to another that he/she prefers. If so, then all the demographic information that is printed on the Aadhaar letter will need to be updated in the new local language.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
UIDAI may also ascertain availability of POI, POA and other documents collected at the time of enrolment/update and its quality and decide to notify Aadhaar number holder to update their demographic information and submit the required document.

Biometric update, the need could arise from:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age <5 years at the time of initial enrolment** -The child should be re-enroled when the child attains an age of 5 years and all biometric data should be provided. A de-duplication would be done for the child at this stage. This request will be treated similar to a new enrolment request while retaining the original Aadhaar number
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age between 5 and 15 years at the time of enrolment** - The Aadhaar number holder should furnish all biometrics for updates when he/she attains age of 15 years.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Age >15 years at the time of enrolment** – Aadhaar number holders are recommended to update their biometric data every 10 years.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Events like accidents or diseases leading to biometric exception
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
As the Aadhaar authentication service is becoming ubiquitous, Aadhaar number holders may also approach for biometric updates because of authentication failures (called false rejects – where a correct Aadhaar number holder with valid Aadhaar number may be incorrectly rejected) which may result from incorrect biometric capture or poor biometric quality captured at the time of enrolment. With improvements in technology, it may be possible to capture better quality biometrics in the CIDR.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
UIDAI may verify the **quality** of biometrics captured during enrolment/ update and decide a threshold quality. All Aadhaar number holders with biometrics below the threshold level would/**will** be notified by UIDAI to update their biometrics

Aadhaar details that can be updated are:  
| Demographic Information  | Name, Address, Date of Birth/Age, Gender, Mobile Number, Email Address, Relationship Status and Information Sharing Consent  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Biometric Information  | Iris, Finger Prints and Facial Photograph  |  
UIDAI update process accepts wide range of PoI (Proof of Identity) and PoA (Proof of Address) documents. View the [List of supporting documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF SIze: 1.6MB.**
Modes of Update
1. Via Online
  
The online mode offers address update to the Aadhaar number holders where the Aadhaar number holder can directly place the address update request on the myAadhaar portal. The Aadhaar number holder needs to have mobile number registered with Aadhaar for using this service. The Aadhaar number is required to login to the [portal](https://myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in/) by the Aadhaar number holder. The Aadhaar number holder is authenticated using sent OTP on his/her registered mobile number. To complete the update process, Aadhaar number holder needs to upload the [supporting POA documents](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/List_of_Supporting_Document_for_Aadhaar_Enrolment_and_Update.pdf) **Doc Type: PDF Size: 1.6MB** , which will be verified against requested data at a later stage by a quality and processing team.
By Visiting Aadhaar Enrolment Centre
Aadhaar number holders place the demographic/biometric update request with the help of an operator at an [Aadhaar Enrolment Centre](https://appointments.uidai.gov.in/easearch.aspx). In such a case, the documentary evidence is collected by the operator at the time of accepting the request. The document verification by the verifier also happens at the time of placing the update request. UIDAI currently has envisaged three modes for Assisted Updates:
a. Update Client Standard
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Fields** : All biometric and demographic fields as well as local language can be updated
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Identity Authentication** : Biometric check at the back-end.

Document Verification
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Enrolment / Update Centre.

Form Filling and Acknowledgement
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Handles spelling, language issues, transliteration, etc. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Update Request Number (URN) which can be tracked.
![Card image](https://backend.uidai.gov.in/get/files/media/document/2026-05/update_client_standard.webp)
b. Update Client Lite (UCL)
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Fields** : All demographic fields and Photo as well as local language can be updated.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
**Identity Authentication** : Biometric Authentication of Aadhaar number holder.

Document Verification
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done for those fields which require documentary evidence
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Verification done by verifier appointed by UIDAI/Registrars present at Aadhaar Enrolment / Update Centre.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The verification procedure followed should be in line with DDSVP Committee Recommendations followed during enrolment process

Form Filling in software and Acknowledgement
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Done by the operator on update client as requested by the Aadhaar number holder. Aadhaar number holder gets an acknowledgement receipt with Enrolment ID (EID) which can be used for checking status. Operator will provide biometric sign off against every update request.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_d34d4322
text:
# Authentication Requesting Agency
Learn about Authentication Requesting Agencies such as AUA and KUA that use UIDAI’s Aadhaar authentication services through ASAs. Explore their appointment process, security requirements, responsibilities and data protection measures for secure identity verification and service delivery.
About Requesting Entities (AUA, KUA)
As per the Aadhaar Act 2016, a requesting entity means an agency or a person that submits Aadhaar number and demographic information or biometric information, of an individual to the Central Identities Data Repository (CIDR) for authentication.
Authentication User Agency (AUA) is an entity engaged in providing Aadhaar Enabled Services to Aadhaar number Holder, using the authentication as facilitated by the Authentication Service Agency (ASA). An AUA may be government / public / private legal agency registered in India, that uses Aadhaar authentication services of UIDAI and sends authentication requests to enable its services / business functions.
**Sub AUAs** are agencies that use Aadhaar authentication to enable its services through an existing requesting entity.
A requesting entity (such as AUA, KUA) connects to the CIDR through an ASA (either by becoming ASA on its own or by contracting services of an existing ASA).
Appointment of Requesting Entities (Authentication User Agency & e-KYC User Agency)
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Agencies seeking to become requesting entities to use the authentication facility provided by the Authority shall apply for appointment as requesting entities in accordance with the procedure as may be specified by the Authority for this purpose. Only those entities that fulfill the criteria laid down in Schedule A are eligible to apply. The Authority may by order, amend Schedule A from time to time so as to modify the eligibility criteria.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The Authority may require the applicant to furnish further information or clarifications, regarding matters relevant to the activity of such a requesting entity, as the case may be, which may otherwise be considered necessary by the Authority, to consider and dispose of the application.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The applicant shall furnish such information and clarification to the satisfaction of the Authority, within the time as may be specified in this regard by the Authority.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
While considering the application, the information furnished by the applicant and its eligibility, the Authority may verify the information through physical verification of documents, infrastructure, and technological support which the applicant is required to have.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
After verification of the application, documents, information furnished by the applicant and its eligibility, the Authority may:
a. approve the application for requesting entity, as the case may be; and  
b. enter into appropriate agreements with the entity or agency incorporating the terms and conditions for use by requesting entities of the Authority’s authentication facility, including damages and disincentives for non-performance of obligations.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The Authority may from time to time, determine the fees and charges payable by entities during their appointment, including application fees, annual subscription fees and fees for individual authentication transactions.

Mandatory Security Requirements
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Aadhaar number should be never used as a domain specific identifier.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
In the case of operator assisted devices, operators should be authenticated using mechanisms such as password, Aadhaar authentication, etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Personal Identity Data (PID) block captured for Aadhaar authentication should be encrypted during capture and should never be sent in the clear over a network.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The encrypted PID block should not be stored unless it is for buffered authentication for a short period, currently configured as 24 hours.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Biometric and OTP data captured for the purposes of Aadhaar authentication should not be stored on any permanent storage or database.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The meta data and the responses should be logged for audit purposes.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Network between AUA and ASA should be secure.

Requesting Entities (AUA/KUA) Responsibilities and Data Securities
For Requesting Entities (AUA/KUA) Responsibilities and Data Securities the Aadhaar Act, 2016 and its regulations may be referred

text:
# Aadhaar Generation
Learn how Aadhaar is generated through quality checks, validation, demographic and biometric de-duplication to ensure uniqueness and secure issuance.
Aadhaar generation & issue
Aadhaar Generation involves process like quality check, packet validation, demographic and biometric de-duplication etc. Aadhaar is generated successfully only if:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Quality of enrolment data meets prescribed standards laid down by UIDAI.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The enrolment packet passes all the validations done in CIDR
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
No Demographic/Biometric duplicate is found

If any of the above conditions is not satisfied, then Aadhaar number will not be issued and the enrolment gets rejected. The processes leading to Aadhaar generation are explained below.
Uploading Enrolment Data to CIDR
Each enrolment data is in a form of software packet which gets encrypted after completion of enrolment in the client itself and is uploaded to the central ID repository (CIDR) using the upload client provided to the Enrolment Agencies by UIDAI. The documents received from individuals seeking to enrol are also scanned and becomes part of enrolment packet which is uploaded to CIDR.
**CIDR Sanity Checks** : Each enrolment packet is exhaustively checked for validity – checksums, packet meta data, etc. – in the CIDR DMZ using automated process before it is moved to the production zone of CIDR for processing.
**Data Archival** : In CIDR, the contents of packet are read and stored in a table before archiving to ensure that the data is kept securely. The archival system has the following requirements:
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
All original packets (enrolments, updates, etc.) are required to be archived as-is, and “forever”, ensuring high availability, and zero data loss
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Archived packet is kept securely and separated from core enrolment and authentication systems.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Archival system may allow on-demand data retrieval with appropriate access control and approvals.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Regular back up of Archived data is taken to ensure zero data loss.

Main Processing Pipeline
After the sanity checks pass, the enrolment packet is passed onto the main processing pipeline. At a high level, this includes the following stages:
CIDR Sanity Checks: Each enrolment packet is exhaustively checked for validity – checksums, packet meta data, etc. – in the CIDR DMZ using automated process before it is moved to the production zone of CIDR for processing.
**Automated Data Validation** : Following validation checks are done in CIDR for demographic data
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Name & Address validations
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Language Validations
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Pincode and Administrative regions
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Regular back up of Archived data is taken to ensure zero data loss.

**Demographic De-duplication** : Demographic De-duplication: Demographic de-duplication is used primarily to catch trivial duplicates (non-fraudulent cases where all the demographic fields are identical) that are inadvertently submitted to the system, e.g., when an individual seeking to enrol has not received Aadhaar number few days after enrolment and decides to re-enrol at an enrolment station again. It is also used to de-duplicate children under the age of 5 year as biometrics data is not captured for children as per UIDAI policy. The goal of demographic de-duplication is to filter these cases and hence reduce the number of trivial duplicates going for biometric de-duplication.
**Manual Quality Checks:** Enrolment packets are sent for manual quality checks, where various quality check operators check the data for demographic and photo quality issues. This includes sanity tests against the individual photo – existence of human image, gross errors in gender and age, gender and photo mismatch as well as issues with the captured data (eg. transliteration errors).
**Biometric De-duplication** : Once a packet passes all validations, and demographic checks, it is sent to the biometrics sub-system for biometric de-duplication. Automated Biometric Identification System ( ABIS) from 3 different vendors is used to ensure the highest levels of accuracy and performance. The vendors are incentivised based on their accuracy and performance to ensure that they continue to improve the performance of their systems. These vendors are provided with individual's anonymized biometrics along with a reference number (generated in CIDR) without disclosing identity of the individuals seeking to enrol. The ABIS system compares the individual's biometrics with all existing biometrics in their gallery to find duplicates, if any.
**Manual Adjudication:** All duplicates identified by ABIS systems are sent to the adjudication module. The purpose of this module is to ensure no individual’s enrolment is rejected due to potential false matches of the ABIS systems.
Aadhaar Issuance
Aadhaar number is allotted after determining the uniqueness of the individual seeking to enrol. The demographics data of individuals seeking to enrol is associated with this Aadhaar number and so it can be used as an identity proof. This information is also sent to the authentication systems, so that authentication of Aadhaar number holder can be performed successfully.
Aadhaar Letter Delivery
After Aadhaar generation, the data is shared with print partner. The print partner is responsible for printing the letter (including tracking information), and delivering it to the logistics partner. The logistics partner (India Post) is then responsible for the delivery of the physical letter to the Aadhaar number holder.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_d6e0cf85
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

text:
### 
How to download the Aadhaar app?
You can download the Aadhaar app on your Android/iOS device from the Play Store/App Store. For Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=in.gov.uidai.pehchaan For iOS: https://apps.apple.com/in/app/aadhaar/id6744029871

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_d782948a
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_d782948a
text:
### 
Which services are available on this app?
Presently, the Aadhaar app offers various services like - Mobile Number Update, Address Update, Biometric lock/unlock, Selective Sharing of Aadhaar Verifiable Credential, check Authentication History, download e-Aadhaar, share Contact Card, Track my request, etc.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_dbf5f320
text:
# Vision and Mission
Vision
To empower Aadhaar number holders of India with a unique identity and a digital platform to authenticate anytime, anywhere.
Mission
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To provide for good governance, efficient, transparent and targeted delivery of subsidies, benefits and services, the expenditure for which is incurred from the Consolidated Fund of India or the Consolidated Fund of State to Aadhaar number holders of India through assigning of unique identity numbers.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To develop policy, procedure and system for issuing Aadhaar number to individuals seeking to enrol of India, who request for same by submitting their demographic information and biometric information by undergoing the process of enrolment.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To develop policy, procedure and systems for Aadhaar number holders for updating and authenticating their digital identity.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Ensure availability, scalability and resilience of the technology infrastructure.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Build a long term sustainable organization to carry forward the vision and values of the UIDAI.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To ensure security and confidentiality of identity information and authentication records of the Aadhaar number holders.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To ensure compliance of Aadhaar Act by all individual and agencies in letter and spirit.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
To make regulations & rules consistent with the Aadhaar Act, for carrying out the provisions of the Aadhaar Act.

Core Values
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We believe in facilitating good governance 
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We value integrity
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We are committed to inclusive nation building
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We pursue a collaborative approach and value our partners
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We will strive towards excellence in services to the Aadhaar number holders and service providers
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We will always focus on continuous learning and quality improvements
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We are driven by innovation and provide a platform for our partners to innovate
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
We believe in a transparent and open organization

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_dd16c37b
text:
### 
How to register on the Aadhaar app?
After downloading the app, the Aadhaar Number Holder (ANH): →Select Language→ Enters their Aadhaar number → Agrees to the Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy → Chooses the SIM card → Performs Face Authentication → Gets registered on the app → Sets a 6-digit PIN to secure access to the app.

title: spider_uidai.gov.in_e2652b8a
text:
# Registrars
Registrar is an entity authorised or recognised by the UIDAI for the purpose of enrolling individuals. They are partner to UIDAI vide a Terms of Engagement (TOE) and responsible for abiding by the roles and responsibilities assigned to them. They are primarily various state governments, central ministries, banks and public sector organizations who have signed TOE with UIDAI for enrolment of individuals seeking to enrol.
How to be a Registrar?
At this stage, the UIDAI has primarily engaged with state governments, central ministries, and financial institutions. The UIDAI has entered into TOE with each registrar where the roles and responsibilities are defined and has to be abided. The signed TOE allows the registrar to start the enrolment of individuals seeking to enrol either on their own or by selection of enrolment agencies.
State and Non State Registrars
The State Government/Union Territory agencies working as Registrar for UIDAI are State Registrar. All the banks and the public sector undertakings who sign a MoU act as Non State Registrar.
Roles & Responsibilities
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Partner with the UIDAI and leverage the ecosystem defined by the UIDAI in implementing the enrolment process
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Only use the software provided by UIDAI for enrolment purpose, which will have the provision of capturing audit data as part of enrolment packet against each enrolment / update for traceability of enrolment client, operator, supervisor, enrolment agency, registrar, and any other information.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
The biometric devices used for enrolment shall meet the specification prescribed by UIDAI as well as certified as per the process prescribed by the Authority.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Engage Enrolment Agencies for enrolment of individuals seeking to enrol, conduct training of the agencies and regular monitoring.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Ensure that standard defined by UIDAI is followed in terms of technology, devices and processes including in training, awareness building, enrolment, authentication etc.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Registrars shall carry the enrolment of individuals seeking to enrol by themselves or through enrolment agencies contracted by them. Registrars shall have option to contract with empanelled enrolment agencies or any other agencies found suitable by them following their own system of contracting such agencies..
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Ensure that all the enrolment packets have been transferred to CIDR within specified time using secured FTP channel only.
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Ensure relevant security protection for data collected during the same; retain safe copies of supporting documents and provide access to UIDAI as and when required
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Partner with Civil Society Organisations and other outreach groups to maximise enrolment of marginalised individuals seeking to enrol
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Setup process for grievance resolution, monitoring EA performance etc. as defined by the UIDAI; provide assistance to UIDAI in resolving matters of dispute

Registrar's Role in Inclusion
The Registrar will have to take special measures to enrol women, children, senior citizens, persons with disability, unskilled and unorganised workers, and nomadic tribes or to such other persons who do not have any permanent dwelling house and such other categories of individuals.
There should be provision on the Registrar front to include all categories of marginalised / vulnerable groups of individuals who have access to one or more of the supporting documents prescribed by UIDAI and other category of individuals seeking to enrol, who cannot provide any document to prove their identity.
To the extent possible Registrar shall have provision for woman operators at institutions where only women are to be enrolled. The Registrar shall also make provision for enrolment of newly born Infants at place of birth like hospitals.
Registrar Activities
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Onboarding of Enrolment Agencies
  * ![arrow](https://uidai.gov.in/assets/svgs/icons/ArrowBullet.svg)
Conduct of training and monitoring of enrolment
